title: Arithmetic lifts and semilinear paths of finite fibre functors
statement:
Let $K$ be a perfect field (every algebraic extension of $K$ is separable), let $L$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $Y=Y_0\times_K L$ [def-pc-base-change], assume $Y$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and choose a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $\bar y_0$ for its composite with $Y\to Y_0$ and $i:L\hookrightarrow\Omega$ for its map of constants. Use the finite etale categories of [def-galois-categories], and let $F=F_{\bar y}$ and $F_0=F_{\bar y_0}$ be their fibre functors [def-galois-fibre-functor]. The structure maps induce homomorphisms as in [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality], and give an exact sequence of profinite groups
$$
1\longrightarrow P:=\operatorname{Aut}(F)\xrightarrow{j}G:=\operatorname{Aut}(F_0)\xrightarrow{r}\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\longrightarrow1.
$$
Give $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ its inverse-limit topology over the finite Galois subextensions of $L/K$. Here $r$ is characterized on the finite constant covers $Y_0\times_K\operatorname{Spec}E$, for finite subextensions $K\subseteq E\subseteq L$, by the action $\tau\mapsto r(g)\circ\tau$ on $\operatorname{Hom}_K(E,L)$, identified with their geometric fibres using $i$. Identify $P$ with its image under $j$.

For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ put $h_\sigma=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma):Y\to Y$. The set $r^{-1}(\sigma)$ is canonically in bijection with the natural isomorphisms
$$
\lambda_s:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar y}.
$$
The bijection is specified by the following evaluation rule, which fixes its inverse convention. For any finite intermediate extension $E/K$ and finite etale cover $Q_E\to Y_E=Y_0\times_KE$, let $Q=Q_E\times_E L$ and let
$$
\iota_\sigma:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E),\qquad
\iota_1:F_{\bar y}(Q)\hookrightarrow F_0(Q_E)
$$
be the injections obtained by forgetting the $L$-structure. The image of $\iota_\sigma$ is the fibre of $Q_E\to Y_0$ whose map of constants $E\to\Omega$ is $i\circ\sigma|_E$, and the image of $\iota_1$ has map of constants $i|_E$. Regard $Q_E\to Y_0$ as a finite etale cover. For every $z\in F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$,
$$
 \iota_1(\lambda_{s,Q}(z))=s^{-1}\cdot\iota_\sigma(z).
$$
This rule is independent of the chosen finite model, and applies to all finite etale $Y$-covers and their morphisms. Via the canonical first-projection identification $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)\cong F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$ for base change [def-pc-base-change], the resulting bijections satisfy
$$
 \lambda_{s,Q}(g\cdot z)=(s^{-1}gs)\cdot\lambda_{s,Q}(z)\qquad(g\in P).
$$
On the left, $P$ acts on $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)$ by evaluation of the fibre functor; on the right it acts on $F_{\bar y}(Q)$. For $a\in P$,
$$
 \lambda_{as,Q}=\lambda_{s,Q}\circ a^{-1}_{h_\sigma^*Q}.
$$
Under the equivalence with finite locally constant sheaves of sets [thm-galois-lc-etale], these are the same natural isomorphisms of stalk functors and the same identities. No coefficient module, descent isomorphism or Weil group is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field (exact sequence and descent to finite separable subextensions); Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit (objects, morphisms and eventual equalities in finite etale covers); Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (fibre-functor actions), and Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group (Galois action on embeddings). The displayed semilinear-path correspondence and normalization are an agent formulation of those finite-fibre constructions, matching the pointed-universal-cover action of Weil II (1.1.12), p.152.

proof.text: For a finite intermediate field $E$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is finite: its algebra is the finite-dimensional $K$-vector space $E$, hence a finite module. It is etale because $K$ is perfect. Finiteness and etaleness survive base change, so $Y_E\to Y_0$ is finite etale. The one-point map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is surjective; its base change $Y\to Y_E$ is therefore surjective. A separation of $Y_E$ into two nonempty clopens would pull back to a separation of the connected $Y$. Thus every $Y_E$, including $Y_0$, is connected. Their basepoints are the composites of $\bar y$.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, first proof paragraph; Tag 0BNE, finite constant covers

proof.text: Construct the quotient map with its precise convention. For a finite Galois intermediate field $N/K$, identify the fibre of $Y_N\to Y_0$ with $\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)$ using $i$. A natural automorphism $u\in G$ commutes with the deck maps, which act on embeddings by right composition. Consequently its permutation is left multiplication by $u_N(1)$: $u_N(\tau)=u_N(1)\tau$. Naturality for projections $Y_{N'}\to Y_N$ makes these left multipliers compatible under restriction. Since $L/K$ is algebraic, normal (minimal polynomials split in the algebraic closure) and separable (perfectness), [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] gives a unique $r(u)\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ with these restrictions. Every finite $E$ is contained in a finite Galois $N$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension], applied to a finite $K$-basis of $E$. Every embedding $E\to L$ is the restriction of an element of $\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$ by the transitivity clause of [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification]. Naturality for the maps of constant covers induced by these embeddings gives $u_E(\tau)=r(u)\circ\tau$ for all $E,\tau$. Composition of these permutations proves that $r$ is a homomorphism. Its finite-coordinate maps are continuous evaluations on finite fibres, hence $r$ is continuous for the specified inverse-limit topology. This also identifies it with the map of structure morphisms: restriction of an automorphism of $F_0$ to the constant covers is exactly that construction.

source.place: Tag 0BNE, lemma-fundamental-group-Galois-group, and Remark 0BQ9, remark-variance; finite-cover construction of the structure homomorphism

proof.text: For each finite Galois $N/K$, the connected cover $Y_N$ is a connected object of the finite etale Galois category, by [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] and [lem-fet-galois-category]. Its fibre is therefore a transitive $G$-set by [lem-galois-transitive]. In the left-translation description of step 2, this says $r_N:G\to\operatorname{Gal}(N/K)$ is surjective. Fix $\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)$. The closed subsets $C_N=\{u:r_N(u)=\sigma|_N\}$ of the compact group $G$ are nonempty. Any finite collection contains the nonempty $C_M$ for a common finite Galois overfield $M$. Thus their intersection is nonempty: otherwise their open complements would cover $G$, and a finite subcover would contradict this finite-intersection property. Any element in the intersection maps to $\sigma$. This proves surjectivity without choosing a compatible family of arbitrary lifts. Compactness here follows from the profiniteness of the fibre-functor automorphism group [lem-galois-aut-profinite].

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, surjectivity paragraph; Tag 0BN3, lemma-tame, applied to each constant cover

proof.text: For each finite intermediate $E$, [thm-galois-fundamental] identifies $\pi_1(Y_E,\bar y_E)$ injectively with the stabilizer $H_E$ of the point $i|_E$ in $F_0(Y_E)$. By step 2, $H_E=\{u\in G:r(u)|_E=\operatorname{id}_E\}$. Under these embeddings, every transition map for $E\subseteq E'$ is the inclusion $H_{E'}\subseteq H_E$: both composites to $G$ act identically on every pulled-back finite cover, by [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality]. Apply [lem-wf-pi1-algebraic-field-limit] with the connectedness proved in step 1. A compatible family in these subgroups is exactly a single element of $\bigcap_E H_E$; its coordinate at $E=K$ is that element. Therefore $j:P\to G$ is injective with image $\bigcap_E H_E=\ker r$. The map $j$ is continuous by functoriality, and is a topological identification with its image by [lem-weil-pbc-compact-hausdorff-bijection], since its domain is compact and its image is a subspace of the Hausdorff group $G$. Together with step 3 this gives the asserted exact sequence of profinite groups.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit, second assertion; Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, geometric kernel and injection

proof.text: For a finite etale $Q_E\to Y_E$, its composite to $Y_0$ is finite etale: finite morphisms compose by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], and etale morphisms compose by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. A point of $Q=Q_E\times_E L$ over $h_\sigma\bar y$ is, by the fibre-product universal property, a point of $Q_E$ over $\bar y_0$ whose $E$-map is $i\circ\sigma|_E$, together with the already fixed constants map $i:L\to\Omega$. Forgetting that second component is injective, and its image is exactly that labelled fibre. For $\sigma=1$ it gives $\iota_1$ and label $i|_E$. Thus the two injections in the statement exist with exactly their stated images; no invariance of $E$ under $\sigma$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0BTX, lemma-ses-field, finite-stage cover construction and its open-and-closed summand; fibre-product interpretation

proof.text: Let $s\in r^{-1}(\sigma)$. Naturality of the automorphism $s^{-1}$ of $F_0$ for $Q_E\to Y_E$ and step 2 show that $s^{-1}$ sends the label $i\sigma|_E$ to $i\sigma^{-1}\sigma|_E=i|_E$. It restricts to a bijection between the two labelled fibres; its inverse is the restriction of $s$. Define $\lambda_{s,Q}$ by that restriction and the injections of step 5. This proves exactly $\iota_1\lambda_{s,Q}=s^{-1}\iota_\sigma$, including the inverse convention.

source.place: Tags 0BNE and 0BQ9, action on embeddings; agent-written restriction of this action to the finite-stage fibres

proof.text: Every finite etale $Y$-cover has a finite model by clause (1) of [lem-wf-finite-etale-field-limit-descent]. If two models represent the same cover, pass to a common finite overfield; clause (2) descends the comparison isomorphism and its inverse, and clause (3) makes their inverse equations hold after further enlargement. Each comparison is then also a morphism of finite etale $Y_0$-covers, so naturality of $s^{-1}$ makes the restrictions in step 6 agree. Enlargement of a model is itself compatible: forgetting to the old model commutes with $s^{-1}$, and on each of the two fixed labelled fibres that forgetting map is bijective by the fibre-product universal property. This proves independence of the model and its identifying isomorphism. For an arbitrary morphism of $Y$-covers, descend it after a common enlargement by clause (2); its $Y_0$-naturality square gives the desired square for $\lambda_s$. Thus these bijections constitute a natural isomorphism on the entire finite etale category, not just on descended morphisms at an initially chosen stage.

source.place: Tag 0BTV, lemma-limit, objects, morphisms and eventual equalities; agent-written compatibility of the restricted arithmetic action

proof.text:
Record precisely how $P$ acts on the two injections. Put $A=Q_E$, regarded as a $Y_0$-cover. There is a morphism of $Y$-covers $Q\to A\times_{Y_0}Y$ using the first projection to $Q_E$ and the structure map to $Y$. There is also a morphism $h_\sigma^*Q\to A\times_{Y_0}Y$ using its projection to $Q$, then $Q_E$, and its own structure map to $Y$; this is over $Y$ since $h_\sigma$ lies over $Y_0$. On fibres at $\bar y$ these maps are precisely $\iota_1$ and $\iota_\sigma$ after forgetting the $Y$-pullback. Naturality and the evaluation identity of [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] therefore give
$$\iota_1(b\cdot x)=j(b)\cdot\iota_1(x),\qquad\iota_\sigma(b\cdot z)=j(b)\cdot\iota_\sigma(z).$$
The second action is on $F_{\bar y}(h_\sigma^*Q)$; the canonical identification with $F_{h_\sigma\bar y}(Q)$ sends a lifted point to its first projection, directly by the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 0BND, theorem-fundamental-group (3), first-projection fibre identification and naturality

proof.text:
Since $P=\ker r$ is normal, $s^{-1}gs\in P$. Using step 8 twice and step 6, compute
$$\iota_1(\lambda_s(gz))=s^{-1}g\iota_\sigma(z)=(s^{-1}gs)s^{-1}\iota_\sigma(z)=\iota_1((s^{-1}gs)\lambda_s(z)).$$
Injectivity of $\iota_1$ proves the required conjugation identity. This is independent of the finite model by step 7 and hence holds on every cover.

source.place: Agent-written group calculation using the fibre actions of Tag 0BND (3)

proof.text:
For $a\in P$, the same restriction calculation gives
$$\iota_1\lambda_{as}(z)=(as)^{-1}\iota_\sigma(z)=s^{-1}a^{-1}\iota_\sigma(z)=\iota_1\lambda_s(a^{-1}z).$$
By injectivity this is $\lambda_{as,Q}=\lambda_{s,Q}\circ a^{-1}_{h_\sigma^*Q}$ with exactly the action specified in the statement.

source.place: Agent-written inverse-product calculation for the normalized arithmetic restriction

proof.text:
It remains to prove that all natural paths are obtained, uniquely. Choose $t\in r^{-1}(\sigma)$, possible by step 3, and let $\lambda:F_{h_\sigma\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F$ be any natural path. Then $b=\lambda\lambda_t^{-1}$ is a natural automorphism of $F$, hence $b\in P$ by definition. Set $s=t b^{-1}\in G$. It has image $\sigma$, and on each finite model
$$s^{-1}\iota_\sigma=j(b)t^{-1}\iota_\sigma=\iota_1 b\lambda_t=\iota_1\lambda.$$
Thus $\lambda_s=\lambda$. If $s'=a s$ is another lift with the same path, step 10 gives $a^{-1}_{h_\sigma^*Q}=1$ on every fibre. Pullback by the scheme automorphism $h_\sigma$ is an equivalence, with inverse pullback by $h_{\sigma^{-1}}$ (the two iterated fibre products identify with the original cover by their projections). Hence $a$ acts trivially on the fibre of every cover, so $a=1$ as a natural automorphism of $F$ and $s'=s$. The construction of the forward map used no chosen $t$, so the bijection is canonical.

source.place: Agent-written torsor argument from natural automorphisms and the explicit finite-model evaluation rule

proof.text: Finally [thm-galois-lc-etale] is an equivalence compatible with base change and the fibre functors. Transport the natural isomorphisms just constructed along this equivalence. Its fibre comparison identifies evaluation on a represented finite etale cover with evaluation on the corresponding finite locally constant sheaf. Consequently the evaluation rule, conjugation equation and lift-change equation become exactly the same equations for stalk functors; they are equalities of the same finite-set maps under these comparisons. This uses only finite locally constant sets, with no coefficient-module or adic extension.

source.place: Stacks finite-locally-constant/finite-etale equivalence and its fibre/base-change compatibility, as recorded in thm-galois-lc-etale

The tags and labels match. I recomputed the conventions myself. In step 2, the permutation is left multiplication u_N(1)τ, which gives r(g)∘τ, and it is a homomorphism. In step 6, s^{-1} moves the label iσ|_E to i|_E. Step 9 gives s^{-1}gs. Step 10 gives λ_{as}=λ_s∘a^{-1}. Step 11: s=tb^{-1} recovers any path λ, and λ_{as}=λ_s forces a=1 because h_σ^* is an equivalence. Every hypothesis holds where it is used: Y_E and Y_0 are connected by step 1; L/K is separable, algebraic and normal because K is perfect; Y_0 is separated of finite type for both limit nodes. The new node lem-wf-pi1-algebraic-field-limit is the second assertion of 0BTV, specialised to the constant-field system. Its extra assumption that X_L is connected is harmless and holds where step 4 uses it. I tested it on L=K and on finite L/K. It has no proof, its searches are recorded, its blueprint fields are correct, it does not restate a clause of the item, and rg over the DAG finds no duplicate of it or of the 0BTX exact sequence. The item is not a duplicate of the finite-field transport and twisted-path nodes either. Accepted tool uses: the six declared ones, and the undeclared generic off-unit Galois-category nodes lem-galois-pi1-functoriality, lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object and lem-fet-galois-category. That is a general scheme fact; neither the trace-formula nor the Poincaré-duality assumption gives it, and it is not a step specific to their proofs, so I judge it outside the assumed statements. No SGA is cited. No fixes.
